title: A Dataset for Uncovering Lazy Thinking in NLP Peer Reviews

bias_targets.methodology: Creating an annotated dataset (LAZYREVIEW) of NLP peer review segments and evaluating the zero-shot, few-shot, and instruction-tuned performance of various LLMs on coarse-grained (binary) and fine-grained (multi-class) classification of superficial reviewing heuristics.

Evaluated as a specific fine-grained category of reviewer lazy thinking ('The results contradict what I would expect') using multi-class classification by LLMs to detect when reviewers reject data contradicting their prior beliefs.

Evaluated as a specific fine-grained category of reviewer lazy thinking ('The results are negative') using multi-class classification by LLMs to detect penalization of papers that report negative results.

Evaluated as a specific fine-grained category of reviewer lazy thinking ('The approach is tested only on [not English]') using multi-class classification by LLMs to detect unfair dismissal of NLP research focusing on non-English languages.

Evaluated as fine-grained categories of reviewer lazy thinking ('Non-mainstream approaches' and 'The paper doesn't use my preferred methodology') using multi-class classification to detect bias against non-deep learning or simpler methods.
